Shares are this community’s count divided by the Maple Ridge total for condos and townhomes that month.

items.t: "Thornhill" is both a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood name and the board sub-area name (listed on the MLS as Thornhill MR, the form the guide page's feed cards carry). The City describes Thornhill as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, with a large mountain-biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street. The City publishes no boundary for the neighbourhood or the MLS sub-area: UNVERIFIED as an official boundary.

Nearby areas: Albion to the southwest, Websters Corners to the southeast, Whonnock to the east, Ruskin further east, and the City of Mission across the eastern boundary. The guide feed's 249 Street cards show the page's scope overlapping Albion on that hillside.
There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Hazards and services: parcel-level ALR, floodplain, well and septic status and wildfire interface mapping for specific streets are UNVERIFIED. Rural properties may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Thornhill Maple Ridge Guide

items.t: Suites and added units: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR parcels the ALR Use Regulation also governs — one secondary suite in the principal residence (s. 31), and an additional residence only if the s. 32 conditions are met.

Pad-rent parks (MHPTA): no manufactured-home park inside Thornhill was verified; where a Maple Ridge park home is bought instead of a strata unit, pad rent may rise at most once every 12 months, on 3 full months' notice, by no more than the yearly limit plus a proportional amount — 2026 = 2.3% plus proportional, 2027 = 2.2% plus proportional. No pad-rent dollar figure is published here.

blocks.text: Good to know about Thornhill Maple Ridge Guide

items.t: Thornhill's entire attached market is one street. Three townhome complexes — The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge — all stand on 248 Street at the sub-area's southwest edge, in a sub-area otherwise made of forested acreage between 248 and 264 Streets; "Thornhill condos" and "Thornhill acreages" are effectively two different markets sharing one board name.
The developer and the board disagree about where Rydge is.

The same 249 Street property appears twice in the guide page's feed at the same price under two MLS numbers (once as Land, once as Residential), so the feed double-counts one parcel; and one feed card's header states an open house of 1:00–3:00 p.m. on November 1, 2026 while the same card's body text states 12:00–2:00 p.m. and then 1–3 p.m. — a one-hour conflict inside one card. No listing address or price beyond this conflict note is republished here.
Zero attached sales in a month with stock on the shelf.

The trail network is the area's signature amenity. The City counts 17 mountain-biking and hiking trails on 256 Street, moderately difficult, typically about an hour each, usable year-round — the 248 Street townhomes sit at the network's southwest corner, and Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls, Bell-Irving Hatchery) is at the west side. Guide-only details recorded as site copy only, UNVERIFIED in the research pass: the Thornhill Park and Hall details and the Thornhill Trails trailhead details quoted on the guide page.

A 500-acre industrial plan touches the north side. The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue — it changes long-term designations around those parcels without approving any construction, and it is a disclosure item for acreage listings in that pocket, not a development approval.
The Lougheed corridor position for this area.
Maple Ridge's OCP citation is unsettled in current sources. The guide page's census snapshot for Thornhill is likewise UNVERIFIED — no Statistics Canada profile figure was opened for the sub-area.

No recreation centre, library branch or shopping centre sits inside this sub-area. The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place), Maple Ridge Public Library (130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Town Centre shopping are all to the west; the serving hospital is Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, with the Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Thornhill
The correct email is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca.
Streets, schools and getting around Thornhill

items.t: All of the attached stock sits at the southwest subdivision edge on 248 Street — The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge — while the rest of the sub-area is freehold acreage.
No townhouse-complex card appears in the guide feed. The exact feed filter criteria beyond those labelled cards: UNVERIFIED.

No superlative is claimed: the detached ratio sits mid-pack among Maple Ridge's twelve sub-areas, and Thornhill is one of only two (with Silver Valley) where attached listings existed but recorded no sale.

Parks, recreation and transit: the City describes Thornhill's 256 Street trail network for mountain biking and hiking — 17 trails, moderately difficult, typically about an hour to complete, usable year-round; Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) sits at the west side, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery; Whonnock Lake Park is in Whonnock to the east. No City recreation centre or library branch sits inside this sub-area; the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and the Maple Ridge Public Library (FVRL), 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre to the west. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Form B diligence (all 3 cross-referenced complexes are strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For Rydge, first establish whether the unit is a developer sale or a resale, because the document route differs. Listing-level rental/pet lines are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Lougheed Corridor: the Lougheed Corridor Area Plan was ADOPTED January 27, 2026 (Bylaw 7781-2021) per the City record — the corridor frame along the sub-area's south side, stated as adopted, not in preparation.

Suites and ALR: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area. On ALR parcels the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: one secondary suite in the principal residence (s. 31), and an additional residence only if the s. 32 conditions are met. ALR status is per-parcel on the ALC map; parcel-level ALR, floodplain, well and septic status and wildfire interface mapping for specific streets are UNVERIFIED. Wells sit in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite sewerage must meet the Sewerage System Regulation's setbacks (including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained).

blocks.text: Good to know about Thornhill

items.t: The guide feed carries no townhouse at all.

The bus is a loop, not a commuter service. Route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) runs weekday and Saturday trips only, at wide intervals, on a long loop through 240 Street, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street — and there is no West Coast Express station in the sub-area. Price the drive into any commute claim for a 248 Street townhouse.

The 256 Street plan area changes designations, not buildings. The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres) at this area's north side — it establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction, so disclose it on nearby listings as a designation change, not a development approval.
Acreage diligence is the real Thornhill checklist.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Thornhill?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 8 condos and townhomes listed in Thornhill. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Thornhill a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Thornhill had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Thornhill from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 2 condos and townhomes sold in Thornhill over those 4 months, out of 184 in all of Maple Ridge.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Thornhill sell for?
faq.a: 7 townhomes sold in Thornhill between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $862,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Thornhill?
faq.a: The median was 19 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 99.3% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How did Thornhill sell in September 2026?
faq.a: Use the Maple Ridge community figures (detached median $1,131,000; attached median $525,000) plus comparable hillside sales.

faq.q: Is Rydge in Albion or Thornhill?
faq.a: Both claims exist in print: Raicon markets it as Albion; its MLS listings say Thornhill MR.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Thornhill townhome long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals can still be restricted; check the registered bylaws on the Form B.

faq.q: What is the Thornhill Urban Reserve, and should I pay for it?
faq.a: The OCP's Urban Reserve designation identifies lands held for long-term future urban services and housing, and OCP policy holds its development until specific triggers and milestones are met — treat it as long-term, not imminent, and do not pay a near-term-development premium on the designation alone.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Thornhill address?
faq.a: Assignment is by exact address through the SD42 School Locator; no catchment is asserted here without a locator run.

faq.q: Is Rydge in Albion or Thornhill?
faq.a: Both claims exist in print: Raicon's own site and the presale record say Albion; its MLS listings say Thornhill MR. A buyer who searches only one name will still be shown the other area's results for this pocket.

faq.q: Terraces or Terraces II — are they one complex?
faq.a: The listing records treat them as two: The Terraces at 10550 248 Street (built 2015) and Terraces II at 10480 248 Street (listings record build years from 2017 to 2019 across its phases), though at least one listing at the 10480 address also uses "The Terraces," and Terraces II's title-level wording is UNCONFIRMED in the listings checked. Confirm the strata plan number for the specific unit on the Form B rather than relying on the marketing name.

faq.q: How did Thornhill sell in September 2026?
faq.a: At the Maple Ridge community level — NOT Thornhill's figures — the detached median was $1,131,000 and the combined attached median was $525,000. Per-sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED.
